subject: Re: Scoped processing & subprocessor audit plan for CCPA/CPRA addendum
messages:
From: Ellen Foster <ellen.foster@brightlinehealth.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Scoped processing & subprocessor audit plan for CCPA/CPRA addendum

Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching Brightline's proposed DPA addendum (Brightline_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf) and a short workbook that maps the current subprocessor list to onshore fallback options (Subprocessor_Audit_Scope.xlsx). Two specific asks from our privacy team: 

1) Scoped processing language: we need a carveout that limits telemetry exports used for platform improvements and clears when aggregated/pseudonymized for analytics. The legal team is ok with limited, transient telemetry if it is not re-identifiable and we can demonstrate deletion timelines.

2) Subprocessor onshore fallback + escrow: because we operate in regulated care, we need a documented plan if any subprocessors cannot provide onshore fallback for California residents. Ideally this includes an audit cadence we can rely on for evidence (quarterly refresh + exception log).

Can Redwood propose specific wording for the scoped telemetry clause and confirm whether you can provide the audit artifacts we requested (SOC-2 scope snippets, KMS attestation, and last 12-month change-log for subprocessors)? We know some of this is sensitive — happy to execute an NDA or Controlled Disclosure Addendum if needed.

Appreciate a short turnaround — our procurement window closes next week.

Best,
Ellen Foster
Head of Privacy Operations
Brightline Health

[Attachment: Brightline_DPA_Addendum_v2.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Subprocessor_Audit_Scope.xlsx (xlsx)]
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Ellen Foster <ellen.foster@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scoped processing & subprocessor audit plan for CCPA/CPRA addendum

Ellen — thanks for the package and for the clarity on timelines. We're aligned on the priority items. High-level answers before I loop in engineering/legal for precise language: 

- Scoped telemetry: we can accept a transient telemetry carveout for platform improvements provided we define: (a) fields that are permitted (metrics, latency, error rates, token counts) and fields that are never stored (raw PII/plaintext content), (b) retention window (default 30 days, auto-delete unless flagged for incident investigation), and (c) pseudonymization approach. We'll propose wording that mirrors what we offer in our Hosted SOC/TEL playbook.

- Subprocessor audit and onshore fallback: Redwood maintains a subprocessor registry and can provide a quarterly snapshot and redaction-friendly SOC-2 summary. For onshore fallback, we have documented fallback options for our telemetry exporters and key subprocessors; where true onshore fallback is unavailable, we offer either: (1) an escrow/rotation plan to bring data to an onshore processor on request, or (2) contractual encryption and key control with customer-managed KMS. We'll outline both options in the draft language.

I'll ask Marissa to draft proposed addendum text and Aditya to gather the audit artifacts you requested. Can you confirm whether Brightline needs full SOC-2 report delivery or a vendor attestation + SOC extracts? That determines our response time.

I'll aim to get a first Redwood redline by EOD tomorrow.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Scoped processing & subprocessor audit plan for CCPA/CPRA addendum

Ellen — looping Neha (privacy operations) and Aditya (infra) as promised. Draft plan and a couple of precise asks below.

Draft plan summary (we will produce redline text):
- Scoped telemetry clause: Redwood proposes to permit aggregated/performance telemetry for service improvement where:
  * Data elements permitted: aggregate token counts, endpoint latency, error-type buckets, anonymized model ID, coarse geolocation by region (US/EU/APAC)
  * Prohibited: any customer content, verbatim PII, or user identifiers that would allow re-identification
  * Retention: 30 days by default; 180 days maximum if flagged for active incident investigation with documented justification and automated purge after resolution
  * Evidence: automated retention records + purge logs exportable for audit (CSV extracts)

- Subprocessor audit/onshore fallback: proposed commitments:
  * Quarterly subprocessor registry snapshot (redacted where appropriate) and a SOC-2 extract for scope items that touch Brightline data flows
  * If onshore fallback is unavailable, option A: short-term escrow/transfer playbook (30–90 day activation window) to move affected telemetry to an onshore provider; option B: customer-managed KMS for telemetry encrypt-at-rest with keys kept in customer KMS and not accessible to Redwood engineers
  * Exception logging: we maintain a timestamped exception log for any subprocessor changes and can provide an exception report on request (redacted as needed)

Two asks for Brightline to confirm so we can finalize wording:
1) For retention, do you require a hard 30-day retention floor or is the 30/180 window above acceptable?
2) For evidence, would a SOC-2 extract + KMS attestation satisfy procurement, or do you need full SOC delivery?

Aditya — can you pull the latest subprocessor snapshot and a short note on KMS options? Neha — can you confirm what our privacy attestation package should include to satisfy a customer procurement review?

Thanks — we should have a clean redline and attachments by EOD Monday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Product & Partnerships, Redwood Inference

- SOC-2 extract: control IDs and control narratives for data handling and incident response (redaction-friendly PDF).
- KMS attestation: confirmation of our use of envelope encryption and options to support customer-managed keys for telemetry buckets.

We also included a proposed activation timeline for onshore fallback (30/60/90 day windows depending on the subprocessor class) in Subprocessor_Audit_Scope.xlsx. If Brightline prefers immediate customer-managed KMS for telemetry, that is available but requires a short onboarding checklist (we've added a one-pager).
